title: A Will for the Parish
premise: August Brightwater, the concierge at the Marlowe Grand Hotel, has built a quiet career on solving guests' small mysteries — until a stranger is found dead in the hotel's chapel garden wearing August's own stolen clothes, and every clue points back to him. The victim turns out to be a private investigator who had been quietly investigating the twenty-year-old disappearance of August's mother, whose will named an unknown heir to the parish's old almshouse estate. As August digs into the case file the investigator left behind, he realizes the killer is someone inside the anniversary dinner circle who has been editing evidence for years. In the end, August stages a trap at the parish's anniversary dinner, forcing a confession before the assembled town, and claims his true identity as the heir his mother hid.
about_author: Jude Dunmore spent a decade working front desks in grand old hotels, collecting the secrets guests leave behind like lost luggage. A Will for the Parish is their third mystery, drawn from a real estate dispute that split a small English town in two.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wore My Coat
chapters.summary: August Brightwater's POV. On the morning of the parish's anniversary preparations, a body is discovered in the chapel garden dressed head-to-toe in clothes missing from August's own closet. Police treat August as a suspect; he treats it as a puzzle. Emotional beat: cold professional calm cracking into personal fear.

chapters.title: Concierge Rules
chapters.summary: August's POV, flashback woven through present interrogation. He explains his unwritten code: notice everything, promise nothing, never take a case you can't close. Detective Inspector Sorrel warns him off. Emotional beat: defiant pride masking how personally the stolen clothes have cut.

chapters.title: Room 412 Left No Footprint
chapters.summary: August's POV. He reconstructs the victim's last days from keycard logs and bellhop gossip: a man calling himself Mr. Vale, who asked odd questions about the hotel's oldest staff. Emotional beat: the thrill of the chase returning, shadowed by grief.

chapters.title: What the Dead Investigator Knew
chapters.summary: August's POV. Searching Vale's room before police seal it, August finds a hidden case file about the 2004 disappearance of Marion Brightwater — his own mother — and her will naming an unnamed heir to the almshouse estate. Emotional beat: vertigo; the case was always about him.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Committee
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Verity Ashcombe, chair of the parish anniversary dinner, as she manages squabbling old families and notices someone has been tampering with the parish archive. Emotional beat: dutiful unease; she recognizes one of August's names from long ago.

chapters.title: Clothes Make the Corpse
chapters.summary: August's POV. Forensics confirm the clothes were taken weeks ago, meaning someone close to him planned this long before. He lists everyone with access to his flat and finds a torn photograph of his mother tucked in a coat pocket. Emotional beat: betrayal turning intimate.

chapters.title: Sorrel's Short Leash
chapters.summary: Alternating August and DI Sorrel POVs. Sorrel, under pressure to charge someone before the anniversary, offers August a devil's bargain: unofficial cooperation in exchange for staying free. Emotional beat: wary alliance, two people who distrust everyone learning to half-trust each other.

chapters.title: The Almshouse Keys
chapters.summary: August's POV. He visits the crumbling almshouse estate from his mother's will and meets its last resident, elderly Mrs. Penhale, who mistakes him for 'the Brightwater boy' and lets slip that Marion came back once, alive, years after she vanished. Emotional beat: hope as a wound reopened.

chapters.title: A File With Missing Pages
chapters.summary: Verity's POV. She compares the parish archive against Vale's case file and finds pages removed — all concerning a fire at the almshouse in 2005. Someone with archive access has been curating the record for decades. Emotional beat: quiet horror of institutional lies.

chapters.title: Everyone Who Loved Her Lies
chapters.summary: August's POV. He interviews the anniversary committee elders who knew his mother; each gives a different account of her final week, each lie polished by twenty years of repetition. Emotional beat: loneliness — found family among hotel staff versus blood family built on falsehoods.

chapters.title: The Understudy
chapters.summary: August's POV. A junior porter, Theo, confesses he was paid to copy August's keys by a voice on the phone — and identifies the payphone location. August realizes the killer used the hotel itself as a weapon. Emotional beat: protective anger; August adopts Theo into his makeshift investigative family.

chapters.title: Smoke and Deeds
chapters.summary: Verity's POV. Digging into land records, she discovers the almshouse estate sits atop land now worth millions, and the anniversary dinner doubles as the reading of a contested bequest. Motive crystallizes: inheritance. Emotional beat: dawning complicity — her own family name is on the deeds.

chapters.title: Dead Man's Voicemail
chapters.summary: August's POV. Vale's phone, recovered from the river, holds one saved message: Marion's voice, recorded in 2019, saying 'If anything happens to me, tell my son who I was.' August learns his mother lived hidden under another identity until recently. Emotional beat: grief upon grief, and fierce new purpose.

chapters.title: The Second Suspect
chapters.summary: Sorrel's POV. Sorrel finds evidence framing August too neatly — planted fingerprints, a staged motive — and concludes the killer wants August charged before the dinner. She begins secretly working the file backwards. Emotional beat: a lawwoman choosing justice over procedure.

chapters.title: Dress Rehearsal
chapters.summary: August's POV. At the anniversary dinner rehearsal, August watches the committee and maps who flinches when the will is mentioned. Mrs. Penhale arrives uninvited and publicly calls one elder by Marion's secret surname. Emotional beat: the mask slipping in public; tension coiling toward detonation.

chapters.title: What Was Taken From Room Nine
chapters.summary: August's POV. Tracing the payphone, August uncovers the killer's safehouse in the hotel's disused ninth floor and finds the missing archive pages — proof the 2005 fire was arson to erase a witness to Marion's first 'death.' Emotional beat: triumph curdling into danger as footsteps sound behind him.

chapters.title: Cornered on the Ninth Floor
chapters.summary: August's POV, near-fatal encounter. The killer — Gerald Ashcombe, Verity's uncle, executor of the estate — reveals he killed Vale and orchestrated the frame because Marion's return threatened to void the inheritance he'd already spent. August escapes through the service lift, wounded. Emotional beat: terror and clarity; the case is closable now, but not safely.

chapters.title: The Trap Is Set
chapters.summary: Alternating August, Sorrel, and Verity POVs. The three conspirators plan to use the anniversary dinner itself: August will announce himself as Marion's heir, forcing Gerald to act before witnesses. Emotional beat: found family assembling — concierge, detective, archivist — each risking what they most value.

chapters.title: Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. August stands before the parish, names himself, and reads the restored pages aloud. Gerald, cornered, moves to silence him with the same ceremonial letter opener displayed beside the anniversary toast. Emotional beat: held breath; performance as survival.

chapters.title: A Toast to the Truth
chapters.summary: Climax. Sorrel arrests Gerald mid-toast as Verity locks down the exits and Theo plays the voicemail recording over the hall speakers — Marion's voice filling the room where her erasure was plotted. Gerald confesses in rage. Emotional beat: catharsis; justice done openly, outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Will
chapters.summary: August's POV. Weeks later, the true will is read: the almshouse goes to August, with a letter from Marion explaining why she hid him — to keep him from exactly this inheritance war. He chooses to turn the estate into housing for hotel workers like Theo. Emotional beat: identity claimed on his own terms.

chapters.title: Never Take a Case You Can't Close
chapters.summary: August's POV, epilogue. Back at the concierge desk, August returns a guest's lost ring, declines a new mystery he knows he can't solve, and keeps his mother's photograph beside the register. Sorrel sends a thank-you note; Verity sends archives; Theo brings tea. Emotional beat: peace earned — the family he found, the name he chose.
